statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 9% while Stress is extreme at 81%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON. NQ trades at 29,431.75, down 0.06%, and has now spent a third consecutive hour inside the 29,364.00-29,508.25 overnight band without extending either edge. The 29,508.25 marginal high printed two hours ago was rejected and price has faded back toward mid-range, so both extremes of the band have produced retracements rather than the persistent no-pullback structure that defines tail conditions. VIX at 16.36, down 0.61% with a 16.29-16.43 range, shows no tail repricing in options, and the 2-year at 4.44% is a basis point lower on the day. Stress stays extreme because Brent at $101.66 has resumed rising after yesterday's brief profit-taking, the 10-year sits near 4.84% after reaching its highest level since November 2023, and roughly 60% odds are priced for a 25 basis point increase on 16 September, with producer prices due today and consumer prices tomorrow. A narrow danger window is published around the 12:30 UTC producer price release and the 13:30 UTC cash open rather than a broad session-wide restriction.
headline: NQ holds 29,431.75 inside an unextended 29,364.00-29,508.25 overnight band for a third hour with VIX easing to 16.36 and the 2-year at 4.44%, while Brent resuming higher at $101.66 and roughly even odds of a September rate increase keep Stress extreme into the 12:30 UTC producer price release
body:
Observed evidence at the assessment cutoff: Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures print 29,431.75, down 17.00 points or 0.06% against a 29,448.75 prior settle, inside an overnight range of 29,364.00 to 29,508.25. That 144.25-point band, roughly 0.49% wide, is now unchanged for a third consecutive hour. The 29,508.25 high was set two hours ago, rejected immediately, never retested, and price has since drifted back to within about 68 points of the band low. Both extremes have therefore produced retracements, and the intervening path has been a fade rather than an extension. That is mean-reverting behaviour, not the persistent directional efficiency that defines tail conditions. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 86.15 points or 0.29%, within a 29,334.40 to 29,563.60 range and beneath a 29,507.70 prior close, a third consecutive lower close for the broader Nasdaq Composite.

Cross-asset conditions remain restrictive, and the energy leg has re-engaged. Brent trades at $101.655, up 0.44%, resuming higher after the brief profit-taking seen in the previous hour and holding near its highest level since 26 May; WTI is $96.64, up 0.61%. The driver is continued US-Iran escalation, including strikes on Iranian oil tankers and attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, with flows through the Strait of Hormuz reported near record lows. The move has so far been gradual rather than disorderly, which matters because an orderly oil repricing transmits to equities as a valuation and margin problem rather than as a liquidity shock. The US 10-year yield reached 4.8568% on 9 September, its highest since November 2023, before settling near 4.835% to 4.846% after a $6 billion Treasury buyback announcement fell short of expectations; the 30-year printed 5.2846% and the 2-year 4.423%, its highest since July 2024. The 2-year has since eased to 4.44%, a basis point lower on the day. VIX is 16.36, down 0.61%, in a narrow 16.29 to 16.43 range. That combination, high macro stress alongside contained and falling implied volatility, is the signature of a difficult but two-way environment rather than a pathological one.

Index internals remain conflicting on latest-session data, with semiconductors firm into early September while megacap leadership has been uneven. Apple's foldable iPhone launch on 9 September saw the shares fall about 2% during the presentation before recovering to close higher, which is dispersion rather than aligned index-level direction. Conflicting internals of this kind reduce directional conviction and raise Stress; they are not evidence of the aligned one-way structure that would justify raising Tail. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run, but its collection timestamp is roughly three hours old and therefore beyond the freshness bound defined by the inherited contract, so it was treated as stale supporting context only and this assessment rests on independently verified current sources.

Scheduled catalysts: August producer prices, core producer prices and weekly jobless claims all release at 12:30 UTC today, with headline producer price consensus near 0.4% month-on-month. August existing home sales follow at 14:00 UTC against consensus near 4.05 million. August consumer prices release at 12:30 UTC on 11 September, and the FOMC decision and projections follow at 18:00 UTC on 16 September, where futures price roughly 60% odds of a 25 basis point increase. None of these had printed at the assessment cutoff, and no outcome is assumed for any of them. Consistent with the risk definition, event importance and forecast dispersion are scored into Stress and Confidence rather than into Tail until an actual price path is observed. Dominant mode is recorded as mixed: range-bound index price action combined with conflicting internals and a restrictive but stable cross-asset backdrop.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 07:00 UTC the mapped policy state was EA_ON in 22 of the 23 available slots, with one WATCH hour at 12:00 UTC on 9 September when Tail reached 20% during a trend-down European session. Tail ranged from 7% to 20% and has held a tight 8-11% band throughout the overnight session as retracements kept appearing at both ends of the range. Stress climbed from 77% to a sustained 80-83% as Brent broke $100 and the 10-year set its highest level since November 2023, then settled at 80% for the last four hours. Confidence held between 87% and 89% throughout. The 10:00 UTC slot on 9 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The published conditional path keeps Tail between 9% and 13% through the European session, lifts it to 20% in the 12:00 UTC release hour and a horizon peak of 22% in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-release repricing would overlap the US cash open, then decays it to 10-17% across the US afternoon and to a 9-12% overnight band into the consumer price session. Only the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots map to WATCH; no slot reaches the 25% block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout because Brent above $100, a 10-year near its highest since November 2023 and roughly even odds of a September rate increase are regime features that a single release does not clear. Confidence decays from 88% to 70% across the horizon as slots move further beyond the observed sample. A narrow danger window is published from 12:25 to 14:00 UTC.
